read.thesis: Gas turbine slot reservations rose to 83 GW (from 62 GW) with pricing on new SRAs 10-20 points above backlog, while 2026 revenue guide was raised to $44-45B and FCF to $5-5.5B.

capex.peers_comment: Management said smaller turbine applications are not seen as competition; no comment on peer capacity.
capex.quote: we remain on track to see a substantial step-up in gas turbine output in 3Q '26.

triggers.label: New SRA pricing 10-20 pts above backlog
triggers.quote: there's another 10 to 20 points of pricing strength in the SRAs today

triggers.label: Gas SRAs + backlog 62→83 GW
triggers.quote: gas power equipment backlog and slot reservations increased from 62 to 83 gigawatts sequentially

triggers.label: 2026 FCF guide raised to $5-5.5B
triggers.quote: We're also increasing our free cash flow guidance to between $5 billion and $5.5 billion, up from $4.5 billion to $5 billion.

triggers.label: Wind EBITDA loss ~$600M vs $400M expected
triggers.quote: Wind losses came in at approximately $600 million, higher than our expectations of approximately $400 million

triggers.label: Wind 1H26 EBITDA loss $300-400M
triggers.quote: we expect EBITDA losses to be between $300 million and $400 million

guidance.quote: we expect full year 2026 revenue to be in the range of $44 billion to $45 billion, up from $41 billion to $42 billion
We continue to expect adjusted EBITDA margins of 11% to 13%
We're also increasing our free cash flow guidance to between $5 billion and $5.5 billion
We anticipate Power EBITDA margins to be between 16% and 18%
we now anticipate revenue to be between $13.5 billion and $14 billion
we expect EBITDA losses to be approximately $400 million in 2026
We now project at least $56 billion of total revenue by 2028, up from $52 billion
cumulative GE Vernova free cash flow generation from '25 to '28 by approximately $2 billion to at least $24 billion

prior_guidance_check.quote: we were talking in the middle of last year at 60 gigawatts and landed at 83 gigawatts
Wind losses came in at approximately $600 million, higher than our expectations of approximately $400 million

red_flags.label: Offshore wind stop-work accrual
red_flags.quote: driven by the U.S. government's December 22 stop work order for offshore wind projects

red_flags.label: Tariff margin pressure on onshore wind 1H26
red_flags.quote: the volume we're shipping in the first half has fewer contractual protections for tariffs

evasions.topic: Electrification organic growth / Prolec margin accretion
evasions.quote: we could have a little bit of a debate as to whether we wanted to change the margin guide
